pillar_reactions.evidence: Presented as functional movement — nine movement patterns against the four a bodybuilding split uses, imbalances from sitting, stabilising and connecting muscles, and realignment of back, legs and shoulder. The prospect volunteered agreement and tied it straight to his own goal: 'No, I would agree, definitely, because I just, I'm not looking for size either, so I'm functional, and getting the stabilizing muscles is big for me, especially getting older.' He then started planning implementation unprompted — 'I'd probably do alternate, maybe do like lifting, and then do the kettlebell... I'd get a best-of-all-world type deal right there' — which is the strongest positive pillar reaction in the batch.

The primal eating protocol was never delivered on this call. The rep pivoted to the Primal University product before reaching it. The prospect had pre-empted it in passing — 'as far as getting down to 10%, when I was running a lot, I'd have to say I probably was at about 10%. So I kind of got a good idea on diet as well' — and no diet question was asked at any point.

Presented only in the negative, as the thing separating the coaching route from the self-serve route: 'there's no feedback. There's no personalization. We're not keeping you accountable.' The prospect pushed back on the substance directly: 'as far as like needing motivation and stuff and doing all that, I... When I lock in, I'm definitely motivated enough. I don't really need all that.' He had also already rejected the delivery mechanism: 'I don't know if I do want to fully go with the online coach as far as like sending in videos.' This is the one clear objected reaction in the batch, and it went unchallenged despite his own account of a lifelong pattern of falling off.

anchors.raw: I used to like bodybuilder.com and get free plans and stuff, but just kettlebells, I just don't, you know, I watch videos, but I don't really have a good grasp on it.
anchors.note: Third call in this batch anchored on free content, and the most explicit. He has a documented history of solving this problem for nothing — 'I've watched a thousand videos', 'I've boughten bodybuilder plans just to kind of compare' — and he found Trevor the same way: 'he has a lot of videos of workouts and stuff. So I was kind of just exploring his page.' Against that baseline, $199 a month for a movement library is being compared to zero.

anchors.raw: I had a friend that quit being an engineer, and he pursued his own fitness journey... started doing custom meal plans, and I kind of had him to lean on a little bit
anchors.competitor: Personal friend working as a fitness coach
anchors.note: He already has informal free access to a professional coach and to a doctor in the family (his brother-in-law, who reassured him about his energy levels). Two of the things the programme sells — expert programming input and health reassurance — he currently obtains at no cost through relationships.

anchors.raw: so the Primal University is $199 per month; for the year it's you save $350 if you sign up so you get like a month and a half free
anchors.note: The only price the prospect ever heard was the cheapest one the company sells, introduced by the rep on the first sign of hesitation. Kettlebell Body was described as 'obviously in the thousands' and never quoted, so the prospect had no premium reference point at all and evaluated $199 as an absolute cost against free alternatives.

anchors.raw: I've always been a do-it-it-myself type of guy
anchors.note: Recorded because its absence is the finding: nothing on this call supported the price. He has never paid for coaching, has no partner or peer in a programme, and explicitly identifies as self-directed. Every anchor available pointed downward.

unmet_demand.want: A structured kettlebell programme and movement library without a coaching relationship — stated three times, including 'I was kind of like looking for a plan with you, with like Trevor' and 'get the plan, get access to the inventory would be the best'.
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Primal University is precisely this and was offered, but it was introduced and priced in under ninety seconds with no value case whatsoever against the free content he already uses, no description of what is inside beyond 'a lot of the same movements', and no answer to the one question he asked about it ('So it's all app-based?' → 'It's on school. So it's on our education platform.').

unmet_demand.want: Confidence that overhead and ballistic kettlebell work is appropriate for a self-rehabbed Bankart shoulder fracture that still limits his pull-ups, and for recurrent sciatica.
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Never addressed. The rep acknowledged the injuries in a single sentence, then discussed progressive overload and 'something snaps' in general terms, and ultimately recommended the option with no form review at all. No clearance question and no adaptation was mentioned.

unmet_demand.want: Resolution of the energy problem he opened and returned to — sluggishness, morning headaches, non-restorative sleep and a suspected breathing issue he links to the 20 pounds.
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The rep drew the thread out well and then let it go without connecting it to anything the programme does. Weight loss is the implied mechanism but was never stated, and the apnoea, which he raised himself, was neither addressed nor referred onward.
